scope_note: Rhee/First Republic remains historical debt; active frontier advances. Floot untouched.

verified_findings.finding: The constitutional order shifted toward a parliamentary cabinet system and bicameral legislature; the Second Republic must be modeled with the President and Prime Minister as distinct authority nodes.
Government proclaimed July 29 as the election date for the 5th House of Representatives and first House of Councillors.
The Democratic Party won 175 of 233 House seats; election disturbances were reported in 13 districts.
A joint session elected Yun Po-sun President 208-51; this office was largely ceremonial under the new system.
Yun's nomination of Kim To-yon was defeated 112-111, exposing old/new faction conflict as a government-formation variable rather than merely a party label.
Chang Myon was confirmed 117-107 and becomes a co-primary executive node for Second Republic research.
Initial cabinet appointments heavily favored the Democratic Party new faction; political backlash produced withdrawals and additional old-faction appointments.
Government appointed Choi Young-hui and Choi Kyung-rok to senior commands; military personnel policy is a necessary pre-May-16 research line.
Democratic Party new faction registered with 95 seats while the old-faction association had 86, confirming institutionalized factional fragmentation.
The Chang government pursued national construction and a 1962-66 five-year economic development draft through the Ministry of Construction; economic planning did not begin ex nihilo after May 16.

CIA reporting later transmitted to President Kennedy recorded coup planning associated with Major General Park Chung-hee before May 16. This is evidence of intelligence reporting, not proof that every Korean constitutional actor received or accepted the same warning.

Contemporaneous U.S. military reporting recorded Chang Do-young calling Magruder around 03:00, describing Park Chung-hee as coup leader and requesting U.S. MPs against ROK Marines; later broadcasts used Chang's name as committee chairman. His precise voluntary/compelled role remains a separate claim.

The U.S. Department of State described restoration of the lawful government as desirable while noting President Yun, military leaders, and other officials were not acting decisively against the coup. This is a contemporaneous U.S. assessment, not a finding of Korean legal responsibility.

adversarial_claims: The Second Republic was politically homogeneous after the July election.
Yun Po-sun exercised the same executive authority as First-Republic presidents.
Chang Myon alone controlled all military personnel decisions.
The Second Republic had no economic-development planning before May 16.
Park Chung-hee's coup plans were wholly unknown before May 16.
Chang Do-young was unambiguously the original voluntary leader of the coup.
U.S. authorities immediately militarily suppressed the coup.
The July 29 election eliminated factional competition inside the Democratic Party.
May 16 can be modeled as a single actor event rather than a sequence of unit, command, political and diplomatic actions.
The military government's July 1961 five-year plan had no policy ancestry in First/Second Republic planning.
